area: LLM/VLM embodied agents: hierarchical planning, memory and 3D scene graphs, embodied QA, uncertainty/failure/safety, small-VLM RL and local-cloud compute routing (scoped to one RTX 5060 8 GB + one real quadruped)

papers.title: Robots That Ask For Help: Uncertainty Alignment for Large Language Model Planners (KnowNo)
papers.venue_year: CoRL 2023, oral (CoRL not in CCF list)
papers.key_idea: Treats LLM planning as choosing among candidate next steps and uses conformal prediction to return a calibrated option set: act if it is a singleton, otherwise ask a human. Statistical task-success guarantees with minimal help; off-the-shelf LLMs, no fine-tuning.
papers.compute_needs: Training-free: needs option likelihoods from an LLM plus a small calibration set. A 4-bit 7B local LLM on one 8 GB GPU suffices (estimate); API LLMs work if log-probs are exposed.
papers.limitation: Assumes an enumerable option set and exchangeable calibration/test data; marginal per-step guarantees; assumes a reliable human helper; shown on instruction-ambiguity manipulation setups, not perception-heavy long-horizon mobile tasks.

papers.title: Introspective Planning: Aligning Robots' Uncertainty with Inherent Task Ambiguity
papers.key_idea: Builds a knowledge base of introspective reasoning examples (post-hoc rationalizations of human-selected safe, compliant plans) retrieved at deployment so LLM uncertainty matches true task ambiguity; with conformal prediction it gives tighter sets, keeps success guarantees and asks fewer unnecessary clarification questions.
papers.compute_needs: Training-free retrieval plus prompting (no fine-tuning mentioned in abstract); API LLM or 4-bit local LLM on 8 GB.
papers.limitation: Text-level plan selection; needs human-labeled safe plans per domain; evaluated on three tasks incl. a new safe mobile-manipulation benchmark, not on legged robots or perception-driven long-horizon agents.

papers.title: Explore until Confident: Efficient Exploration for Embodied Question Answering
papers.key_idea: Builds a depth-based semantic map whose exploration values come from VLM visual prompting, and calibrates the VLM's answer confidence with conformal prediction so the robot stops once confident. Contributes an HM3D-based EQA dataset (used by later work as HM-EQA).
papers.compute_needs: Training-free apart from a small calibration set; original used an open VLM (Prismatic-VLM per GraphEQA), so a 4-bit 7B-class VLM on one 8 GB GPU is plausible (estimate).
papers.limitation: 2D semantic map, single-floor scenes, fixed step budget; GraphEQA reports GPT- and Llama-based re-implementations become overconfident and stop early, so calibration does not transfer across VLMs.

papers.title: OpenEQA: Embodied Question Answering in the Era of Foundation Models
papers.key_idea: First open-vocabulary EQA benchmark: 1,600+ human-written questions from 180+ real environments in two settings, episodic-memory EQA (answer from recorded egocentric history) and active EQA (explore to answer), scored with an LLM-based match metric.
papers.compute_needs: Evaluation-only. EM-EQA needs only VLM inference over frames; A-EQA runs in Habitat-sim with HM3D scenes; both fit one 8 GB GPU with quantized small VLMs (estimate); GPT-4 judge needs API calls.
papers.limitation: LLM-judge scoring adds noise and cost; static indoor scenes at human height; A-EQA often evaluated on small subsets (184 questions in 3D-Mem), so few-point gains can be within noise.

papers.title: SayPlan: Grounding Large Language Models using 3D Scene Graphs for Scalable Robot Task Planning
papers.key_idea: LLM performs semantic search over a collapsed hierarchical 3D scene graph, expanding only task-relevant subgraphs; a classical path planner shortens the LLM horizon; iterative replanning with scene-graph-simulator feedback repairs infeasible actions. Shown in environments up to 3 floors, 36 rooms, 140 objects and on a real mobile manipulator.
papers.compute_needs: Training-free; strong LLM via API plus CPU graph search and path planning; GPU only needed if a local LLM replaces the API.
papers.limitation: Assumes a pre-built, accurate, static 3D scene graph; prompt tokens grow with environment size (later addressed by EmbodiedRAG, arXiv 2410.23968); no handling of perception or execution uncertainty.

papers.title: Hierarchical Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graphs for Language-Grounded Robot Navigation (HOV-SG)
papers.key_idea: Builds open-vocabulary 3D maps from RGB-D with OpenCLIP (ViT-H-14), segments them into floors and rooms, names rooms, and forms a floor-room-object hierarchy for language-goal navigation in multi-story buildings; 75% smaller than dense open-vocabulary maps.
papers.compute_needs: Training-free offline mapping with foundation-model inference; fits 8 GB but slow on large scenes (estimate). Needs posed RGB-D.
papers.limitation: Static offline construction without online updates or change handling; depends on good depth and poses; not coupled to an LLM agent loop or uncertainty estimates.

papers.title: 3D-Mem: 3D Scene Memory for Embodied Exploration and Reasoning
papers.key_idea: Memory Snapshots (multi-view images chosen by co-visibility clustering of detected objects) plus Frontier Snapshots for unexplored regions; a VLM picks a snapshot to answer or a frontier to explore, with class prefiltering. A-EQA 52.6 LLM-Match, EM-EQA 57.2, GOAT-Bench 69.1% SR (GPT-4o).
papers.compute_needs: Training-free with GPT-4o API plus YOLOv8x-World detector (fits 8 GB). The open LLaVA-1.5-7B variant needed LoRA fine-tuning on a multi-V100 setup (~6 h) and is much weaker (49.6% SR on GOAT-Bench).
papers.limitation: No multi-floor support; misses small objects at 360x360 VLM input; detector mislabels; VLM overconfidence causes early stops; frontier oscillation; relies on habitat-sim navmesh; evaluated on subsets for cost; no latency reported.

papers.title: GraphEQA: Using 3D Semantic Scene Graphs for Real-time Embodied Question Answering
papers.venue_year: CoRL 2025, PMLR v305 (CoRL not in CCF list)
papers.key_idea: Real-time Hydra metric-semantic 3D scene graph plus task-relevant images as multimodal memory; hierarchical VLM planner picks room, then object nodes and semantically tagged frontiers, outputs answer plus confidence and stops above a threshold. Beats Explore-EQA and SayPlanVision on HM-EQA and OpenEQA with fewer steps; real Stretch RE2 runs.
papers.compute_needs: Training-free. Planners were GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Pro or Llama 4 Maverick (too large for 8 GB), so local use needs a smaller VLM or an API; Hydra resource needs not reported.
papers.limitation: Hinges on VLM confidence calibration (baselines were overconfident); no latency, hardware or cost figures despite the real-time claim; needs RGB-D and accurate poses; wheeled Stretch only, no legged robots.

papers.title: ReMEmbR: Building and Reasoning Over Long-Horizon Spatio-Temporal Memory for Robot Navigation
papers.key_idea: Memory-building phase stores VILA video captions with embeddings, positions and timestamps in a vector database; a querying phase runs an LLM agent loop over it to answer where/when/how-long questions and output navigation goals. Introduces NaVQA (210 examples, videos up to 20 min); deployed on a Nova Carter robot.
papers.compute_needs: Training-free. Captioner and vector DB can run locally (a small VILA on 8 GB is plausible, estimate); best results used GPT-4o, so local LLMs trade accuracy.
papers.limitation: Caption-only memory loses geometry and visual detail (confused soda machines with water fountains); static-world assumption without memory update or forgetting; small dataset; wheeled robot only.

papers.title: Explore with Long-term Memory: A Benchmark and Multimodal LLM-based Reinforcement Learning Framework for Embodied Exploration (MemoryExplorer)
papers.key_idea: Defines Long-term Memory Embodied Exploration: the agent accumulates episodic memory during multi-goal navigation, then memory-based QA tests recall and decision-making jointly. MemoryExplorer RL-fine-tunes a multimodal LLM to actively query memory, improving recall and proactive exploration.
papers.compute_needs: Requires RL fine-tuning of an MLLM (GPU budget not verified; likely multi-GPU). Evaluating small quantized VLMs on the benchmark should fit 8 GB (estimate).
papers.limitation: Base model, rewards, simulator and any real-robot results not verified (CVF PDF returned 403); check before citing numbers.

papers.title: Enter the Mind Palace: Reasoning and Planning for Long-term Active Embodied Question Answering (LA-EQA)
papers.key_idea: Defines Long-term Active EQA: a robot running for days to months answers time-dependent questions by combining recall of past experience with new exploration. Episodic memory stored as scene-graph-based world instances (mind-palace inspired); a value-of-information stopping rule balances recall versus exploring.
papers.compute_needs: Training-free reasoning with large models (unnamed on abstract page); scene-graph memory is lightweight. Feasible with an API VLM plus local mapping (estimate).
papers.limitation: Abstract gives no models, robot platform or numbers; benchmark mixes simulation and real industrial sites; assumes reliable 3D perception and object re-identification over long periods (inference).

papers.title: EmbodiedBench: Comprehensive Benchmarking Multi-modal Large Language Models for Vision-Driven Embodied Agents
papers.key_idea: 1,128 test tasks in four environments spanning high-level semantic tasks (EB-ALFRED, EB-Habitat) and low-level atomic actions (EB-Navigation, EB-Manipulation), with capability subsets (commonsense, complex instructions, spatial awareness, visual perception, long-horizon). Of 24 MLLMs, best GPT-4o averages only 28.9% on low-level manipulation.
papers.compute_needs: Evaluation-only; simulators plus a quantized 3B-7B VLM fit one 8 GB GPU (estimate); frontier models via API.
papers.limitation: Simulated household/tabletop only; high-level tasks use discrete skill APIs; no legged, outdoor or real-robot component; now a common RL target (ERA, RoboGPT-R1, RoboMemory), so incremental gains there are less novel.

papers.title: ERA: Transforming VLMs into Embodied Agents via Embodied Prior Learning and Online Reinforcement Learning
papers.venue_year: arXiv Oct 2025 (OpenReview forum exists; decision not verified)
papers.key_idea: Stage 1 Embodied Prior Learning from trajectory-augmented (stronger-model reasoning), environment-anchored and external-knowledge data; stage 2 online RL with self-summarization for context, dense reward shaping and turn-level policy optimization. ERA-3B beats GPT-4o by 8.4 points on EB-ALFRED and 19.4 on EB-Manipulation.
papers.compute_needs: SFT plus online RL of a 3B VLM with simulator rollouts; GPU budget not on abstract page. 3B inference fits 8 GB; full online RL on 8 GB is unlikely without heavy LoRA and short-context compromises (estimate).
papers.limitation: Simulation-only (EmbodiedBench); priors are environment-specific; no real-robot, legged or outdoor validation.

papers.title: Embodied-R1: Reinforced Embodied Reasoning for General Robotic Manipulation
papers.key_idea: Uses pointing as an embodiment-agnostic intermediate representation linking VLM understanding to action primitives (four pointing abilities); trains a 3B VLM on Embodied-Points-200K with two-stage reinforced fine-tuning and multi-task rewards. SOTA on 11 spatial/pointing benchmarks; 56.2% zero-shot on SIMPLEREnv; 87.5% on 8 real XArm tasks.
papers.compute_needs: R1-style RFT on ~200K samples (multi-GPU; budget not on abstract page). The 3B model's inference fits 8 GB, so it can serve as a local pointing/grounding module (estimate).
papers.limitation: Tabletop manipulation; pointing needs depth and calibration to become actions; no navigation, memory or legged-robot evaluation.

papers.title: Thinking in Space: How Multimodal Large Language Models See, Remember, and Recall Spaces (VSI-Bench)
papers.key_idea: VSI-Bench: 5,000+ QA pairs over 288 egocentric videos from ScanNet, ScanNet++ and ARKitScenes. MLLMs show emerging but sub-human visual-spatial intelligence; spatial reasoning is the main bottleneck; probing via self-explanations and cognitive maps reveals local world models.
papers.compute_needs: Evaluation-only; quantized 2B-7B open VLMs can be evaluated on 8 GB; frontier models via API.
papers.limitation: Indoor, static, human-carried video; later work (arXiv 2512.19683) finds gains vanish in open-world settings and models lean on language priors; no active perception.

papers.title: SpaceR: Reinforcing MLLMs in Video Spatial Reasoning
papers.venue_year: arXiv Apr 2025 (OpenReview forum exists; venue unconfirmed)
papers.key_idea: SpaceR-151k (91k verifiable spatial QA plus 60k general) and SG-RLVR, a GRPO variant with map imagination that makes the model infer layouts while reasoning. Beats GPT-4o by 11.6% on VSI-Bench, on par with Gemini-2.0-Flash; SOTA on STI-Bench and SPAR-Bench.
papers.compute_needs: GRPO training of a video VLM (base model and compute not on abstract page; typically multi-GPU). Released data allow LoRA/GRPO replication on a smaller model; 4-bit inference fits 8 GB (estimate).
papers.limitation: Indoor static video QA only; rewards restricted to verifiable answers; no closed-loop embodiment; gains may partly reflect benchmark shortcuts.

papers.title: Cambrian-S: Towards Spatial Supersensing in Video
papers.key_idea: Curates VSI-590K spatial instruction data for about 30-point absolute VSI-Bench gains without hurting general skills; introduces VSI-SUPER (long-horizon recall and counting) and predictive-sensing inference, arguing scale alone does not yield spatial supersensing.
papers.compute_needs: Large-scale MLLM training (multi-GPU). VSI-590K metadata (released Apr 2026) can support LoRA fine-tuning of a small VLM on 8 GB (estimate).
papers.limitation: arXiv 2511.16655 shows a bag-of-words SigLIP baseline gets 95% on VSI-Super-Recall and replaying each video twice drops Cambrian-S counting from 42% to 0%: shortcut-prone evaluation; passive video, no action.

papers.title: AHA: A Vision-Language-Model for Detecting and Reasoning Over Failures in Robotic Manipulation
papers.key_idea: Open-source VLM that treats failure detection as free-form reasoning: it detects manipulation failures and explains them in language across robots, tasks and sim/real; its failure reasoning improves downstream VLM systems (Trust the PRoC3S, Manipulate-Anything, Eureka).
papers.compute_needs: Fine-tuned VLM (training data and size not verified here); inference likely needs 4-bit quantization to fit 8 GB (estimate).
papers.limitation: Manipulation-only, mostly reactive post-hoc detection; no navigation or locomotion failures (stuck, lost, wrong room); no calibrated confidence.

papers.title: Code-as-Monitor: Constraint-aware Visual Programming for Reactive and Proactive Robotic Failure Detection
papers.key_idea: Casts open-set failure detection as spatio-temporal constraint satisfaction: relevant objects/parts become constraint elements, a VLM writes monitor code checked in real time, and violations trigger explanations and replanning; covers reactive (unexpected) and proactive (foreseeable) failures.
papers.compute_needs: Mostly VLM code generation plus cheap runtime checks; any trained perception component not verified. Pattern fits a local GPU running checks while an API VLM writes code (estimate).
papers.code: Project page linked from paper (not verified)
papers.limitation: Cluttered tabletop manipulation; depends on accurate part-level perception and on the VLM writing correct constraints; no navigation or legged failure modes.

papers.title: Safety Guardrails for LLM-Enabled Robots (RoboGuard)
papers.key_idea: Two-stage guardrail: an isolated root-of-trust LLM grounds predefined safety rules in the robot's environment via chain-of-thought into temporal-logic specifications; temporal-logic control synthesis reconciles them with possibly unsafe plans, minimally overriding user intent. Unsafe plan execution under worst-case jailbreaks falls from over 92% to below 3%.
papers.compute_needs: Training-free; one LLM call plus temporal-logic synthesis on CPU; resource-efficient per authors.
papers.limitation: Plan-level only; needs a semantic world model and hand-written rules; no guarantees at locomotion/control level; evaluated mainly against jailbreaks, not perception errors.

papers.title: Sibyl: an efficient small-large model collaboration framework for long-horizon tasks
papers.key_idea: Adds a call_cloud action to an on-device SLM (Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B): self-evolving RL with skill-conditioned distillation, cold start on decisive-disagreement states, then consultation-aware RL with counterfactual credit. ALFWorld 95.2-97.4% success with 0.3-0.8 cloud calls per episode; API cost 21-44x lower than cloud-only.
papers.compute_needs: Trained on 8 AMD MI308X GPUs, ~150-206 GPU-hours plus ~105-146 USD API spend. 0.6B-1.7B inference fits 8 GB easily; a scaled-down LoRA replication may be feasible (estimate).
papers.limitation: Text-only ALFWorld/WebShop, no vision or physical robot; exact-state credit matching will not transfer to continuous visual states; fixed cloud policy; Pareto curves from single checkpoints.

papers.title: DIRECT: When and Where Should You Allocate Test-Time Compute in Embodied Planners?
papers.key_idea: Test-time compute is not a uniform lever: chain-of-thought depth, model size and memory length help different capabilities. A router picks a compute level per prompt from multimodal scene context, beating any fixed model on the success-cost Pareto front; on a real robot it matches a stronger model at up to 65% lower latency.
papers.compute_needs: Router is lightweight; planners are VLMs of several sizes (unnamed on abstract page). Maps directly to a local small VLM on the 8 GB GPU plus an API large VLM.
papers.limitation: Manipulation only (VLABench, RoboMME, Franka DROID setup); no calibrated error guarantee on routing; no mobile/legged robots or long-horizon memory.

papers.title: WildLMa: Long Horizon Loco-Manipulation in the Wild
papers.venue_year: arXiv Nov 2024, v2 Mar 2025 (venue not listed)
papers.key_idea: Quadruped with manipulator: learned whole-body controller for VR teleoperation and traversability; WildLMa-Skill library of visuomotor skills via CLIP-conditioned imitation learning or heuristics; WildLMa-Planner lets an LLM chain skills for long-horizon tasks (hallway/outdoor trash pickup, articulated objects, shelf rearrangement).
papers.compute_needs: Skills need tens of demonstrations each (imitation learning, likely single-GPU scale, estimate); LLM planner is training-free API use.
papers.limitation: Requires an arm on the quadruped and VR teleop data; planner is a thin skill interface without memory, uncertainty or failure recovery; long-horizon results mostly qualitative.

papers.title: Binary Tracking for Spatial QA and Navigation with Open Vision-Language Models (BinTrack, GangnamLoop)
papers.key_idea: Open-source localization agent: finds two anchor landmarks from the query, binary-searches the trajectory between them and outputs a metric coordinate for navigation. Introduces GangnamLoop, multi-trip outdoor street data from a real quadruped pairing robot and owner viewpoints. Up to +22.8% over open agents; GPT-4o-level on SpaceLocQA global; over 1.5x faster.
papers.compute_needs: Training-free with open VLMs (sizes not on abstract page); designed to avoid closed-model network latency and cost, i.e., local/onboard GPUs.
papers.limitation: Relies on ordered single trajectories and distinctive landmarks; outdoor street domain; no exploration, change detection or calibrated abstention.

papers.title: Talk2Escape: Conversational Grounding for Vision-and-Language Navigation
papers.key_idea: Model-agnostic wrapper: a lightweight vision-language monitor detects looping or large drift and turns egocentric views into short grounded questions to an oracle or human whose corrections recover the run. 66.0% SR on R2R-CE; gains on RxR-CE and VLNVerse; sim-to-real on a Unitree Go2 quadruped.
papers.compute_needs: Lightweight monitor on top of existing VLN agents; monitor-style add-ons are 8 GB-friendly (estimate).
papers.limitation: Needs an oracle or human to answer; no calibrated policy for when to ask; VLN only (no memory/EQA); monitor model and onboard compute unspecified.

benchmarks.name: OpenEQA (EM-EQA and A-EQA)
benchmarks.simulator: EM-EQA: offline recorded egocentric episodes; A-EQA: Habitat-sim with HM3D scenes
benchmarks.metrics: LLM-Match (GPT-4 judge); LLM-Match x SPL for exploration efficiency
benchmarks.sota_note: 3D-Mem (GPT-4o): 52.6 LLM-Match / 42.0 SPL on a 184-question A-EQA subset, 57.2 on EM-EQA; HIMM (IROS 2026) reports +7.3% LLM-Match and +11.4% LLM-Match x SPL; GraphPad 55.3% on OpenEQA; humans about 85-87.
benchmarks.gpu_needs: Eval-only; Habitat-sim plus a quantized 3B-7B VLM fits one 8 GB GPU (estimate); judge needs API calls.

benchmarks.name: HM-EQA (Explore-EQA dataset)
benchmarks.metrics: Answer success rate (multiple-choice), VLM planning steps, trajectory length
benchmarks.sota_note: GraphEQA (CoRL 2025) beats Explore-EQA and SayPlanVision with fewer planning steps; exact numbers not captured here.

benchmarks.name: GOAT-Bench (multi-goal, multi-modal navigation)
benchmarks.sota_note: 3D-Mem: 69.1 SR / 48.9 SPL with GPT-4o and 49.6 / 29.4 with LLaVA-7B on a Val-Unseen subset; HIMM reports +7.7 SR and +6.8 SPL.
benchmarks.gpu_needs: Eval-only; sim on one consumer GPU; VLM via API or quantized local model.

benchmarks.name: EmbodiedBench (EB-ALFRED, EB-Habitat, EB-Navigation, EB-Manipulation)
benchmarks.simulator: Four simulated environments (household ALFRED-style, Habitat rearrangement, navigation, tabletop manipulation); exact engines not verified here
benchmarks.metrics: Task success rate per environment and per capability subset
benchmarks.sota_note: At release GPT-4o averaged 28.9% on low-level manipulation; ERA-3B +8.4 (EB-ALFRED) and +19.4 (EB-Manipulation) over GPT-4o; RoboGPT-R1 (Qwen2.5-VL-3B) +21.33% over GPT-4o-mini; RoboMemory (Qwen2.5-VL-72B) +26.5% average SR over its baseline.
benchmarks.gpu_needs: Eval-only fits 8 GB with 3B-7B quantized VLMs (estimate); online RL training needs more.

benchmarks.name: VSI-Bench (and VSI-SUPER)
benchmarks.simulator: None: offline egocentric videos from ScanNet, ScanNet++, ARKitScenes
benchmarks.metrics: Accuracy (multiple-choice) and mean relative accuracy (numerical); VSI-SUPER recall and counting
benchmarks.sota_note: SpaceR +11.6% over GPT-4o; Video-R1-7B 37.1%; Cambrian-S about +30 points absolute; Cambrian-P +4.5-6.5. Shortcut critique (arXiv 2511.16655) and open-world gap (arXiv 2512.19683) weaken leaderboard claims.
benchmarks.gpu_needs: Eval-only; 8 GB enough for quantized 7B or smaller VLMs; LoRA training on small models feasible (estimate).

benchmarks.name: ERQA (Embodied Reasoning QA)
benchmarks.simulator: None: multimodal multiple-choice questions over robotics images
benchmarks.sota_note: Released with Gemini Robotics (Mar 2025); Gemini Robotics-ER 1.5 (arXiv 2510.03342) reports state-of-the-art embodied reasoning; ERQA-Plus (arXiv 2606.17639) adds 1,766 questions over 711 images.
benchmarks.gpu_needs: Eval-only; trivially fits 8 GB with small VLMs.

benchmarks.name: NaVQA (ReMEmbR)
benchmarks.simulator: None: real long-horizon robot navigation videos (up to 20 min)
benchmarks.metrics: Per question type (spatial, temporal, descriptive) with type-specific outputs; exact metrics per paper
benchmarks.sota_note: ReMEmbR with GPT-4o best at release; VL-KnG (arXiv 2510.01483) reports frontier-VLM-competitive accuracy at lower, history-independent query latency.
benchmarks.gpu_needs: Eval-only; captioner plus retrieval fits 8 GB (estimate).

benchmarks.name: FindingDory and EMem-Bench (long-term embodied memory)
benchmarks.simulator: FindingDory: Habitat, 60 memory-dependent navigation+manipulation tasks, procedurally extendable; EMem-Bench: 2,554 interactive episodes in four task families (simulator not verified)
benchmarks.metrics: Task success after memory-dependent recall and action
benchmarks.sota_note: FindingDory: VLMs struggle beyond a few hundred images; EMem-Bench (Sep 2026): models weak and uneven, EMem memory system and EMem-8B best.
benchmarks.gpu_needs: Small-model eval fits 8 GB; long image histories stress VRAM, motivating retrieval.

benchmarks.name: SafeAgentBench
benchmarks.simulator: SafeAgentEnv (custom embodied environment, 17 high-level actions, multi-agent capable)
benchmarks.metrics: Hazardous-task rejection rate, success on safe tasks, execution and semantic evaluation
benchmarks.sota_note: 750 tasks, 10 hazard categories, 3 task types; safest of 9 baselines rejects only 10% of detailed hazardous tasks; swapping the LLM barely helps.

benchmarks.name: IS-Bench (interactive safety)
benchmarks.metrics: Process-oriented safety: risk-mitigation steps before/after risk-prone actions; task completion
benchmarks.sota_note: 161 scenarios, 388 risks; GPT-4o and Gemini-2.5 show weak interactive safety; safety CoT raises safety but lowers completion.

benchmarks.name: ALFWorld (text embodied; used for local/cloud cascades)
benchmarks.simulator: Text-based household environment aligned with ALFRED
benchmarks.metrics: Success rate (Seen 140 / Unseen 134 games), cloud calls per episode, API cost
benchmarks.sota_note: Sibyl-1.7B 97.4% with 0.3 calls/episode vs Gemini 3.1 Pro cloud-only 98.6% with 9.1 calls; 96.3% on Unseen.

benchmarks.name: SpaceLocQA and GangnamLoop (spatial localization QA)
benchmarks.simulator: None: SpaceLocQA (prior benchmark) and GangnamLoop (real quadruped, multi-trip outdoor streets, low robot view plus owner view)
benchmarks.sota_note: BinTrack: up to +22.8% over open-source agents, matches GPT-4o agents on SpaceLocQA global, over 1.5x faster.
benchmarks.gpu_needs: Open VLM inference; designed for local/onboard compute.

trends: Memory representations diversify beyond object-only 3D scene graphs: image snapshots (3D-Mem), 3DSG plus images (GraphEQA), API-editable scene graph plus scratchpad (GraphPad), spatiotemporal knowledge graphs from monocular video without 3D reconstruction (VL-KnG), episodic/semantic split with rule extraction (HIMM).

Long-term, changing-world memory is the new evaluation frontier: LA-EQA (days to months), NaVQA, FindingDory, MemoryExplorer (CVPR 2026), EMem-Bench (Sep 2026) and memory-centric EQA (MemoryEQA, arXiv 2505.13948) show VLM agents degrade with long histories and state changes.

R1-style RL on small VLMs: SFT/distillation then GRPO-like RL with verifiable or shaped rewards lets 3B-7B models beat GPT-4o on narrow embodied tasks (Embodied-R1, ERA-3B, SpaceR, Video-R1, Embodied-R, RoboGPT-R1, EmbodiedBrain Step-GRPO).

Open embodied-brain VLMs as local backbones: RoboBrain 2.0 (7B/32B, BAAI; 2.5 follow-up), Cosmos-Reason1-7B (NVIDIA, physical-AI SFT+RL); closed Gemini Robotics-ER 1.5 leads embodied reasoning. 7B-8B open models need 4-bit quantization on 8 GB.

Compute- and latency-aware reasoning: deciding when and how much to think and when to call a bigger model per step (DIRECT up to 65% lower latency; RARRL 'When Should a Robot Think?'; PACE hides 66.8% of thinking time in execution; Sibyl call_cloud 21-44x cheaper; StepGate for tool agents).

Calibration and abstention: conformal lineage KnowNo, IntroPlan, Explore-EQA, multi-robot CP planning, CommCP (2026), conformal fine-tuning of planners (arXiv 2511.06575); AbstainEQA and step-level calibrated frontier selection (Prune-Then-Plan, CVPR 2026 Findings-track URL) target when to stop or refuse.

Embodied safety: jailbreaks of LLM-controlled robots (arXiv 2410.13691, POEX) motivate guardrails (RoboGuard) and interactive safety benchmarks (SafeAgentBench, IS-Bench, AGENTSAFE); agents still rarely refuse hazardous tasks.

Failure handling moves from detection to recovery: AHA, Code-as-Monitor, Guardian (self-generated failure data), Dream2Fix counterfactual failure synthesis (correction 19.7% to 81.3%), AgenticLab real-world closed-loop benchmark; nearly all manipulation-centric.

Spatial-intelligence benchmarks saturate and get contested: large VSI-Bench gains (Cambrian-S, SpaceR) but shortcut attacks on VSI-SUPER and an open-world gap, pushing toward streaming/active evaluation (AMF-VLM, arXiv 2603.23864) and embodied tests.

Legged-robot agent work is growing but thin: NaVILA (RSS 2025) VLA-to-locomotion, WildLMa LLM skill chaining, Talk2Escape on Go2, GangnamLoop quadruped data, GuideDogQA on-device guide-dog perception (83.8% vs GPT-4o 67.1%), CoopSR two-quadruped cooperative spatial reasoning; multi-robot LLM planning (COHERENT, RoboOS).
open_gaps: Calibrated local/cloud VLM cascades on a physical agent: Sibyl is text-only, DIRECT is manipulation-only without guarantees, KnowNo escalates to humans. No verified work gives risk-controlled per-step escalation from a local VLM to an API VLM on a real mobile robot with cost reporting (check RACER, cited by StepGate, before claiming theory novelty).

Long-term memory under change for a legged robot: multi-floor (stairs), indoor-outdoor, multi-day memory with change detection, forgetting and re-identification. 3D-Mem lacks multi-floor, ReMEmbR assumes static captions, FindingDory/EMem-Bench are simulated; real legged long-term EQA data is scarce.

Quadruped-viewpoint perception: VSI-Bench and OpenEQA use human-height, smooth video; effects of low camera height, gait shake and motion blur on VLM spatial reasoning and memory are largely unmeasured (GangnamLoop covers outdoor localization only).

Navigation-level failure detection and recovery: AHA, Code-as-Monitor and Dream2Fix are manipulation-centric; mobile/legged agent failures (stuck, looping, wrong room, target lost, unsafe terrain) lack a benchmark and calibrated detectors; Talk2Escape only detects looping/drift and asks an oracle.

Calibrated stopping and abstention in active EQA: GraphEQA and 3D-Mem report VLM overconfidence and early stopping; Explore-EQA's calibration does not transfer across VLMs; few methods keep coverage guarantees under sim-to-real or model shift.

Physical-risk-aware guardrails for mobile legged agents in human spaces (stairs, people, pets, doors): RoboGuard is plan-level and SafeAgentBench/IS-Bench are household simulations; no legged or real-world interactive safety benchmark found.
Cost reporting: GraphEQA and 3D-Mem report no latency or cost; a standard accuracy-latency-tokens-dollars protocol on edge hardware is missing and would itself be a useful contribution.

Memory retrieval tuned for small models: VLMs struggle beyond a few hundred images (FindingDory); retrieval and compression policies learned or calibrated for 3B-7B local models are underexplored versus GPT-4o pipelines.
low_compute_entry_points: Training-free wrappers on open code: fork 3D-Mem, GraphEQA, Explore-EQA or ReMEmbR; swap GPT-4o for a 4-bit 3B-7B local VLM; add calibrated escalation to an API VLM; evaluate on A-EQA/HM-EQA/GOAT-Bench subsets, all inference-only on one 8 GB GPU.

Conformal risk control for escalation: calibrate per-step thresholds on cheap simulator episodes to bound the local model's wrong-answer or wrong-action rate; a theory-backed contribution without large-scale training.

Small-model RL with LoRA: GRPO on a 1.5B-3B VLM with narrow verifiable rewards (stop-or-explore, frontier choice, memory retrieval). Unsloth reports text GRPO on Qwen2.5-1.5B in about 7 GB and VLM GRPO support for Qwen2.5-VL, but lists a 16 GB T4 for Qwen3-VL-8B; rent cloud GPUs for bigger runs.

Collect a small real quadruped long-term dataset (multi-day, multi-floor, indoor-outdoor loops with QA and change annotations) from the dog's own low camera; it doubles as a benchmark contribution and real-robot validation.
Eval-and-analysis study: dog-view vs human-view robustness (height, shake, blur) of small VLMs on VSI-Bench/OpenEQA-style questions; inference-only, fits 8 GB.

Navigation failure monitor in Code-as-Monitor style: a local small VLM writes or runs runtime checks (progress, looping, target visibility) and escalates to an API VLM for replanning; build a failure set from logged real-dog runs plus Habitat.

Treat the M1 as camera + odometry + velocity/waypoint commands (ROS or vendor SDK) with heavy models on the RTX 5060 desktop over Wi-Fi; first check sensors, since HOV-SG/GraphEQA need RGB-D and poses, while VL-KnG/ReMEmbR-style memory can work from monocular video.

Environment setup: Ubuntu 20.04 with system Python 3.8 is too old for current VLM stacks; use Docker or conda with Python 3.10+ and a PyTorch build supporting Blackwell sm_120 (CUDA 12.8+ wheels; verify before installing).

Implication: robotics venues (ICRA, IROS, CoRL, RSS) do not count as CCF-A; an embodied-agent paper should target CVPR, ICCV, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, AAAI or ACM MM.

candidate_topics: Risk-controlled local/cloud VLM cascade for long-horizon EQA and object search on a quadruped: 4-bit 3B-7B VLM on the RTX 5060 plus conformal per-step escalation to an API VLM; report accuracy, calls, latency and cost on A-EQA/HM-EQA/GOAT-Bench subsets and the real M1. Differs from Sibyl (text-only) and DIRECT (no guarantee). Targets: CVPR/ICCV/NeurIPS/AAAI.

Dog-view long-term memory benchmark plus method: multi-day, multi-floor, indoor-outdoor recordings from the low camera with change-aware QA; a memory agent with change detection and calibrated abstention; small-VLM LoRA/GRPO only for retrieval or stop decisions. Targets: CVPR/ICCV (dataset+method) or ACM MM.

Agent-level failure monitoring for legged navigation: VLM-generated runtime checks, a failure taxonomy and dataset from real M1 runs plus Habitat, recovery by replanning; compare with Talk2Escape-style asking. Targets: AAAI/CVPR.
hardware_fit_notes: Measured reference: StepGate reports local peak memory of 990 / 3003 / 6058 MiB for Qwen2.5 0.5B / 1.5B / 3B text models.

Estimates (not measured): a 4-bit 7B VLM needs about 5 GB for weights plus vision tokens and KV cache, fitting 8 GB at short context; a BF16 3B VLM is tight, so use 8- or 4-bit; QLoRA SFT of 1.5B-3B VLMs should fit; multi-rollout GRPO on a 3B VLM is borderline.
Batch-1 decode is memory-bandwidth bound (arXiv 2605.30571), so call the VLM at decision points rather than every frame, and run cheap checks or detectors in between.
Full online RL as in ERA or Embodied-R1, and 7B-class GRPO as in SpaceR, should go to rented cloud GPUs; keep the 8 GB card for inference, LoRA and evaluation.
